summary: This experimental document specifies extensions to Generic Aggregate RSVP from RFC 4860 to support the PCN Controlled Load and Single Marking edge behaviors over a Diffserv cloud.

eli5.summary: This RFC adds extra rules so a network can admit traffic only when it has enough room.

questions: how does pcn admission control work
how does single marking flow termination work
when would you use pcn in a network
subtitle: RSVP extensions for admitting traffic based on network congestion signals.

tldr.problem: Networks need to admit new traffic flows only when they have capacity, and to drop flows when congestion approaches, but traditional RSVP does not work well across large Diffserv domains without detailed per-flow state.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC extends Generic Aggregate RSVP (RFC 4860) to work with Pre-Congestion Notification (PCN), which marks packets before actual congestion occurs. PCN signals let edge routers admit new flows or terminate overload flows with aggregate messages instead of per-flow signaling.
tldr.outcome: Networks can manage admission and overload without tracking thousands of individual flows, enabling scalable QoS in large service domains.

today: RFC 7417 is an Experimental specification. It has not been obsoleted or updated, and deployment of PCN with aggregate RSVP remains a research area.

sections.title: Aggregate RSVP for Pre-Congestion Control
sections.content:
RFC 7417 combines two technologies. RSVP (Resource ReSerVation Protocol) lets applications request a guaranteed quality of service. Pre-Congestion Notification (PCN) is a simple signaling scheme where interior routers mark packets when traffic gets close to saturation, without actually dropping them.

The problem: traditional RSVP requires every router to maintain state for every flow, which does not scale in a large network. Generic Aggregate RSVP (RFC 4860) groups many flows and makes aggregate reservations, reducing state. RFC 7417 adapts this for PCN: when a PCN-marked packet reaches a boundary router, that router knows congestion is building, and it can use PCN marks to decide whether to admit new flows or terminate existing ones.

This approach works within a Diffserv domain—a region of the network using a common QoS policy—and is Experimental.
sections.eli5: Traffic reservation (RSVP) is like booking a lane at the pool. Aggregate RSVP books one lane for many swimmers. Pre-congestion notification is like a lifeguard saying "the pool is getting crowded" before people start bumping into each other.

sections.title: PCN Marking and Edge Behaviors
sections.content:
PCN works by marking packets at interior routers when traffic approaches link capacity, before actual congestion. Interior routers count PCN-marked bytes to measure load; edge (boundary) routers see those marks and take action.

RFC 7417 specifies two edge behaviors: Controlled Load (CL) and Single Marking (SM).

Controlled Load: The edge router admits a new flow request only if the aggregate traffic with PCN marks stays below a threshold. The router makes an aggregate RSVP Path message claiming enough bandwidth to carry all the flows it is admitting, and the interior routers reserve capacity for that aggregate.

Single Marking: When congestion marks appear, the edge router can decide to terminate certain flows. A single PCN mark level signals approaching congestion, triggering controlled flow termination.

Both behaviors reduce the need for per-flow state in the core: only edge routers need to track end-to-end flows.
sections.eli5: Controlled Load is saying "I will let more swimmers in only if the water is calm." Single Marking is "When the water gets choppy, I will ask some swimmers to leave."

sections.title: RSVP Message Handling and Aggregation
sections.content:
When an end-to-end (E2E) flow request arrives at a PCN ingress router (the edge of the domain), the ingress router decides whether to admit it based on local PCN measurements. If admitted, the ingress router creates an aggregate RSVP Path message to the egress router (deaggregating router), grouping many E2E flows together.

Interior routers forward the aggregate Path message like any RSVP message, marking packets and recording congestion marks. At the egress router, the Resv (reservation confirmation) message is created and sent back. The egress router detects when PCN marks on egress traffic exceed configured thresholds and, in Single Marking mode, tells the ingress router to terminate certain flows.

Throughout, the RFC specifies precise handling of Path and Resv messages at each router type (ingress, interior, egress), including procedures for multicast sessions, removal of reservations, and handling of misconfiguration.
sections.eli5: When a swimmer wants to book a lane (E2E flow), the gate attendant (ingress router) checks if the pool is calm. If yes, the attendant tells the main office (interior network) "reserve space for this group." If marks appear, the attendant calls the swimmer out.

sections.title: Protocol Objects and Extensions
sections.content:
RFC 7417 introduces new RSVP objects: PCN Objects that carry PCN-related parameters in RSVP messages. These objects specify admission control thresholds, flow termination policies, and the mapping between E2E and aggregate flows.

Key fields include parameters for Controlled Load edge behavior (admission thresholds for PCN-marked traffic) and Single Marking behavior (congestion thresholds that trigger flow termination). The RFC defines these objects at IANA, allowing future extensions.
sections.eli5: PCN Objects are like forms the gate attendant fills out to tell the system "admit only if marks are below this level" or "ask swimmers to leave if marks exceed this level."

sections.title: Scalability and Experimental Status
sections.content:
RFC 7417 enables QoS management in networks too large for per-flow RSVP: a domain with thousands of flows can manage admission with a few aggregate reservations and simple marking signals. The tradeoff is that only flows at the edge are visible to admission control; interior routers see only aggregates.

The RFC is Experimental. IANA registries for the PCN Objects allow future Controlled Load or Single Marking variants. The signaling approach—E2E Path aggregation, mark-based termination, and multi-level aggregation—is tested in this version.

Deployment requires PCN support at all interior routers in the domain, coordinated configuration of marking and admission thresholds, and support from edge routers for both RSVP and PCN processing.
sections.eli5: This works best when the whole pool (the network domain) uses the same rules. It is still being tested, so future versions might add more types of markers or behaviors.
